title: Transposable Elements Seed Transcription Factor Binding Sites to Sequence-Specific Double-Stranded DNA Binding TF Networks Contributing to Governance of Primate Brain Evolution.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究转座子为转录因子提供结合位点并塑造灵长类脑发育调控网络，涉及TF-DNA结合位点但主要基于基因组序列与表达分析，缺乏AI或物理模拟方法，属于广义TF-DNA互作背景文献。
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) have played a pivotal role in shaping the regulatory architecture of mammalian genomes. This contribution reports multiple lines of evidence suggesting that TE have made a significant impact on brain development by providing sequences for thousands of transcription factor binding sites (TFBS). TE-encoded TFBS have scaffolded brain developmental regulatory regions (BDRRs) across mammalian evolution. TFBS density within BDRRs has markedly increased along the evolutionary trajectory from mouse to macaque to chimpanzee, reaching its highest levels in modern humans. This density increase is accompanied by the preferential selection of specific TFs that actually bind genomic regulatory sequences. Consequently, humans and chimpanzees exhibit distinct repertoires of BDRR-bound TFs, which contribute to divergent developmental trajectories across hundreds of brain regions ranging from subcortical to telencephalon structures, including the basal ganglia (12 regions), midbrain (48), thalamus & prethalamus (85), hindbrain & cerebellum (25), limbic system & amygdala (25), neurodevelopmental structures (26). Despite the diversity of sequences contributed by different TEs, they encode TFBS for a relatively small set of ~ 700 TFs that act as central nodes organizing these regulatory landscapes. This provides a unifying framework for understanding both conserved and species-specific patterns of primate brain development. It suggests that TF networks seeded by TEs are key drivers of human neurodevelopmental innovation. Differential enrichment analyses of human vis-a-vis chimpanzee BDRRs identified 25 human BDRR-bound TFs that emanate transcriptional signatures of small TF subsets with significantly increased expression in 202 neuroanatomical structures. These observations point to a regulatory paradigm that small sets of highly-expressed genes that are significantly enriched in distinct human brain regions are selected from genes encoding TFs bound to human-specific BDRRs, thus linking "neuroanatomical transcriptional signatures" of brain structures to TFs governing brain development. Together, our findings highlight TE-derived TFBS as central architects of primate brain evolution, providing both mechanistic insight and avenues for future discovery.
abstract_zh: 转座元件（TEs）在塑造哺乳动物基因组调控架构中发挥了关键作用。本报告提供了多条证据线，表明转座元件通过为数千个转录因子结合位点（TFBS）提供序列，对大脑发育产生了显著影响。TE编码的TFBS在哺乳动物进化中支撑了大脑发育调控区域（BDRRs）的构建。从小鼠到猕猴再到黑猩猩的进化轨迹中，BDRRs内的TFBS密度显著增加，在现代人类中达到最高水平。这种密度增加伴随着实际结合基因组调控序列的特定转录因子（TFs）的优先选择。因此，人类和黑猩猩展现出不同的BDRR结合TFs谱系，这导致了从皮层下结构到端脑结构（包括基底节（12个区域）、中脑（48个）、丘脑与前丘脑（85个）、后脑与小脑（25个）、边缘系统与杏仁核（25个）、神经发育结构（26个））等数百个大脑区域的分化发育轨迹。尽管不同TEs贡献的序列具有多样性，但它们编码的TFBS对应于相对较小的约700个TFs集合，这些TFs作为组织这些调控景观的核心节点。这为理解灵长类大脑发育的保守性和物种特异性模式提供了一个统一框架，表明由TEs引发的TF网络是人类神经发育创新的关键驱动因素。人类与黑猩猩BDRRs的差异富集分析识别出25个人类BDRR结合的TFs，这些TFs在202个神经解剖结构中产生显著表达增加的小型TF子集的转录特征。这些观察指向一种调控范式：在人类特定大脑区域显著富集的少量高表达基因，是从编码结合人类特异性BDRRs的TFs的基因中选出的，从而将大脑结构的“神经解剖转录特征”与调控大脑发育的TFs联系起来。总之，我们的发现强调了TE衍生的TFBS作为灵长类大脑进化的核心建筑师，既提供了机制性见解，也为未来发现开辟了途径。
